scope: All 102 Voice Path lessons, connected to bundled Suede Sing practice studies and authored reading with native self-check completion.

instructionConventions.practiceTiming: Segment durations sum to catalog minutes and include setup, rests, review, and recovery. They are attention blocks, not competence deadlines or continuous-phonation requirements.
instructionConventions.comfort: Use repeatable comfortable pitches and moderate intensity. Stop for pain, burning, sudden hoarseness, loss of range, or a speaking-voice change. Persistent symptoms need a qualified clinician, not another app attempt.
instructionConventions.measurement: Native lesson completion records self-observed practice. Synthesized reference patterns demonstrate note targets; they do not measure the singer. The separate range tool provides its own limited detected-pitch view.
instructionConventions.selfReport: Register, break continuity, vowel consistency, diction, articulation, dynamics, passaggio, belt safety, improvisation quality, vibrato, ornament identity, style, production weight, effects, and harmony remain human judgments where the app has no validating measurement.
instructionConventions.referenceAudio: Reference playback supplies a target, not evidence of the singer. Stop it before recording or judging microphone input.
instructionConventions.healthBoundary: These lessons teach practice decisions and stop rules. They do not diagnose, treat, medically clear, or certify freedom from strain or injury.

integrationNote.catalogInventory: The Voice catalog publishes 102 actual lesson objects across 34 modules. This resource authors those objects only; it does not invent the 135 additional lessons implied by lessonsTotal fields.
integrationNote.proofBoundary: Voice lesson self-checks do not produce cents, timing, melody, vocal-health, strain, or register scores.
integrationNote.loader: LessonInstructionLibrary.loadBundled must merge voice-instruction after the three guitar instruction resources.
integrationNote.reviewBoundary: A qualified vocal pedagogy and clinical-safety review remains required before presenting advanced belt, weight, range-extension, or effects guidance as professionally reviewed instruction.
integrationNote.nativeMaterial: voice-learning-material.json bundles existing Suede Sing exercises, public-domain song notation, and owned chapter text. Module IDs connect every lesson to its included material. No companion subscription or external purchase is required.

lessons.title: Why Loud Playback Ruins Pitch
lessons.objective: Reference sound can enter the microphone along with your voice. Compare your setup with playback stopped.

steps.title: Use your included practice material
steps.action: Open Practice material and choose Sustained hold. Hear the reference, choose a comfortable key, then stop it before singing. The reading What your voice actually is is included here; no separate purchase is needed.
steps.lookCheck: The study or chapter is open in this lesson. Your chosen range remains comfortable.
steps.listenCheck: Synthesized pitches supply the notes; they are not recordings of a singer demonstrating a technique.

steps.title: Set a safe baseline
steps.action: Silence reference playback, lower speaker volume below halfway, and use wired headphones when available. Keep the microphone opening clear and stay one relaxed hand-span away.
steps.lookCheck: Posture, room, device, and the planned stop rule are settled before the first attempt.
steps.listenCheck: Begin from an easy, repeatable sound; silence playback before judging your own voice.

steps.title: Name the target: Room setup and clean input
steps.action: Reference sound can enter the microphone along with your voice. Compare your setup with playback stopped. Say what will count as complete in this lesson before practising, and keep the attempt inside the range and duration you can repeat comfortably.
steps.lookCheck: The recording starts with your voice, settles while you sing, and returns to quiet instead of moving with playback or room noise.
steps.listenCheck: Your recorded voice is clear enough to follow without echo, clipping, a second voice, or loud accompaniment.

steps.title: Hear the distinction
steps.action: Make two brief, comfortable examples of the idea in “Why Loud Playback Ruins Pitch.” Change only the named variable. Record both contrast examples in one take with a quiet breath between them, then return to the easier baseline. Saving a new take replaces this lesson’s previous recording. Make one comfortable sustained sound, then leave a full quiet gap before the next. Change only one room or device setting at a time so you can hear what fixed the input.
steps.lookCheck: The recording starts with your voice, settles while you sing, and returns to quiet instead of moving with playback or room noise.
steps.listenCheck: Your recorded voice is clear enough to follow without echo, clipping, a second voice, or loud accompaniment.

steps.title: Review your own attempt
steps.action: I compared a quiet recording with my initial room setup and could hear my voice clearly. Compare your attempt with the supplied material and choose one smaller adjustment for next time.
steps.lookCheck: Note the pitch, key, or setup you used so that your next comparison is useful.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for the specific change taught in this lesson. Saving a self-check records your reflection, not an automatic vocal score.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The target disappears when the range, volume, speed, or duration increases.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: If the recording includes the speaker or room noise, stop playback, move away from noise, and try one fresh sound.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The reference and your own sound seem different, or you cannot judge the result.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Treat the reading as missing, not as a pass or failure. Stop reference audio, restore a quiet setup, make one easier fresh attempt, and keep the human listening judgment separate from the measurement.

practiceSegments.instruction: Open your included Practice material. Prepare the room, body, and safe baseline for “Why Loud Playback Ruins Pitch.”
Isolate the room setup and clean input target in short, comfortable examples.
Practise or record the complete “Why Loud Playback Ruins Pitch” task, resetting between attempts.
Review one take against the stated listening goal and write the next smaller correction.

criteria: I compared a quiet recording with my initial room setup and could hear my voice clearly.
Your recorded voice is clear enough to follow without echo, clipping, a second voice, or loud accompaniment.
I kept missing or uncertain evidence as missing instead of awarding myself a measured pass.

selfAssessment.ifNotReady: If the recording includes the speaker or room noise, stop playback, move away from noise, and try one fresh sound. Repeat a smaller version on another fresh attempt rather than forcing the checkpoint.

lessons.title: Low First, High Second, Neither Forced
lessons.objective: Comfortable, not extreme. The number we want is the one you can use.

steps.title: Use your included practice material
steps.action: Open Practice material and choose First hum or Easy fourth siren. Hear the reference, choose a comfortable key, then stop it before singing. The reading Reading your range test is included here; no separate purchase is needed.
steps.lookCheck: The study or chapter is open in this lesson. Your chosen range remains comfortable.
steps.listenCheck: Synthesized pitches supply the notes; they are not recordings of a singer demonstrating a technique.

steps.title: Set a safe baseline
steps.action: Start near the middle of your comfortable speaking range after a gentle hum. Keep the jaw loose and choose a small lip trill, hum, or easy vowel rather than a loud call.
steps.lookCheck: Posture, room, device, and the planned stop rule are settled before the first attempt.
steps.listenCheck: Begin from an easy, repeatable sound; silence playback before judging your own voice.

steps.title: Name the target: Range scan and voice type
steps.action: Comfortable, not extreme. The number we want is the one you can use. Say what will count as complete in this lesson before practising, and keep the attempt inside the range and duration you can repeat comfortably.
steps.lookCheck: Keep the supplied reference or reading visible, settle your posture, and use only a pitch and duration you can repeat comfortably.
steps.listenCheck: Both slides remain conversational in effort. The last usable note sounds repeatable, not like an extreme reached once.

steps.title: Hear the distinction
steps.action: Make two brief, comfortable examples of the idea in “Low First, High Second, Neither Forced.” Change only the named variable. Record both contrast examples in one take with a quiet breath between them, then return to the easier baseline. Saving a new take replaces this lesson’s previous recording. Glide down only while the sound stays easy, reset, then glide up separately. Stop before squeezing, pain, scratchiness, or the urge to reach for a number.
steps.lookCheck: Keep the supplied reference or reading visible, settle your posture, and use only a pitch and duration you can repeat comfortably.
steps.listenCheck: Both slides remain conversational in effort. The last usable note sounds repeatable, not like an extreme reached once.

steps.title: Review your own attempt
steps.action: I tried a comfortable low and high note without forcing either end and noted the pitches I could repeat. Compare your attempt with the supplied material and choose one smaller adjustment for next time.
steps.lookCheck: Note the pitch, key, or setup you used so that your next comparison is useful.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for the specific change taught in this lesson. Saving a self-check records your reflection, not an automatic vocal score.

lessons.title: Ribs Out, Shoulders Still
lessons.objective: What to move and what to leave alone.

steps.title: Use your included practice material
steps.action: Open Practice material and read Breath: support versus pressure. Use its written exercise and stop rules. The reading Breath: support versus pressure is included here; no separate purchase is needed.
steps.lookCheck: The study or chapter is open in this lesson. Your chosen range remains comfortable.
steps.listenCheck: For the breathing or planning task, follow the written exercise; you do not need to make a pitched sound.

steps.title: Set a safe baseline
steps.action: Stand or sit tall without locking the ribs. Let the shoulders remain quiet while the lower ribs and abdomen respond to an unforced inhale.
steps.lookCheck: Posture, room, device, and the planned stop rule are settled before the first attempt.
steps.listenCheck: Begin from an easy, repeatable sound; silence playback before judging your own voice.

steps.title: Name the target: Low breath and rib expansion
steps.action: What to move and what to leave alone. Say what will count as complete in this lesson before practising, and keep the attempt inside the range and duration you can repeat comfortably.
steps.lookCheck: The shoulders do not rise sharply, the neck stays quiet, and the body does not fold during the final seconds.
steps.listenCheck: The hiss stays even rather than surging at the start and fading to almost nothing at the end.

steps.title: Hear the distinction
steps.action: Make two brief, comfortable examples of the idea in “Ribs Out, Shoulders Still.” Change only the named variable. Record both contrast examples in one take with a quiet breath between them, then return to the easier baseline. Saving a new take replaces this lesson’s previous recording. Release a narrow, even hiss. Favor steadiness over duration, and end with air still available instead of collapsing or bearing down.
steps.lookCheck: The shoulders do not rise sharply, the neck stays quiet, and the body does not fold during the final seconds.
steps.listenCheck: The hiss stays even rather than surging at the start and fading to almost nothing at the end.

steps.title: Review your own attempt
steps.action: I counted an even hiss, kept my shoulders quiet, and released before running out of comfortable breath. Compare your attempt with the supplied material and choose one smaller adjustment for next time.
steps.lookCheck: Note the pitch, key, or setup you used so that your next comparison is useful.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for the specific change taught in this lesson. Saving a self-check records your reflection, not an automatic vocal score.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The target disappears when the range, volume, speed, or duration increases.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: If the hiss pulses or rushes out, use less air, shorten the attempt, rest for a normal breath, and repeat at an easier duration.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The reference and your own sound seem different, or you cannot judge the result.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Treat the reading as missing, not as a pass or failure. Stop reference audio, restore a quiet setup, make one easier fresh attempt, and keep the human listening judgment separate from the measurement.

To hear a flat 7 below the tonic, lower the study’s Key setting by two semitones, hear its first note, then restore the original Key. Choose a key above the control’s lowest setting so that this adjustment is available. Stop the reference and tap four steady beats per bar; no backing loop is needed.
steps.lookCheck: Posture, room, device, and the planned stop rule are settled before the first attempt.
steps.listenCheck: Begin from an easy, repeatable sound; silence playback before judging your own voice.

steps.title: Name the target: Eight-bar improvisation
steps.action: Rung two of the ladder. Say what will count as complete in this lesson before practising, and keep the attempt inside the range and duration you can repeat comfortably.
steps.lookCheck: The eight bars have a clear form with room to breathe; bends are optional and never forced.
steps.listenCheck: The take keeps the tapped pulse, develops one repeated idea, and resolves by ear to the tonic you heard before recording.

steps.title: Make one evidence take
steps.action: State the checkpoint target, record one uninterrupted attempt, and keep the result even when it does not pass. Use blue thirds and sevenths as deliberate destinations, not pitches reached by accidental flatness. Leave space and repeat a motif before varying it. Begin with a two-bar call: sing 1, flat 3, 5, rest, then 5, flat 3, 1, rest, one event per tapped beat. Answer with flat 7 below the tonic, 1, flat 3, rest, then flat 3, 1, 1, rest. Repeat those four bars with one rhythmic change to make eight. At the starting Key of −12, those pitches are C3, E♭3, G3, and B♭2; transpose the whole exercise if needed. Record the call and answer together in one take.
steps.lookCheck: The eight bars have a clear form with room to breathe; bends are optional and never forced.
steps.listenCheck: The take keeps the tapped pulse, develops one repeated idea, and resolves by ear to the tonic you heard before recording.

steps.title: Review your own attempt
steps.action: I used the supplied minor and pentatonic patterns to make my own short answering phrases. Compare your attempt with the supplied material and choose one smaller adjustment for next time.

steps.listenCheck: Listen for the specific change taught in this lesson. Saving a self-check records your reflection, not an automatic vocal score.

steps.action: I rehearsed the supplied study arrangement and compared microphone distance or phrasing on separate takes. Compare your attempt with the supplied material and choose one smaller adjustment for next time.
steps.lookCheck: Note the pitch, key, or setup you used so that your next comparison is useful.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for the specific change taught in this lesson. Saving a self-check records your reflection, not an automatic vocal score.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The target disappears when the range, volume, speed, or duration increases.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: If the harmony collapses into the lead, mute the lead, sing the harmony from its anchor notes, then restore the lead at lower volume.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The reference and your own sound seem different, or you cannot judge the result.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Treat the reading as missing, not as a pass or failure. Stop reference audio, restore a quiet setup, make one easier fresh attempt, and keep the human listening judgment separate from the measurement.

practiceSegments.instruction: Open your included Practice material. Prepare the room, body, and safe baseline for “Self-Check: Your Performance Study.”
Isolate the performance and harmony target in short, comfortable examples.
Practise or record the complete “Self-Check: Your Performance Study” task, resetting between attempts.
Review one take against the stated listening goal and write the next smaller correction.

criteria: I rehearsed the supplied study arrangement and compared microphone distance or phrasing on separate takes.
On playback, the harmony keeps its own contour and the full song remains complete from first entry to release.
I kept missing or uncertain evidence as missing instead of awarding myself a measured pass.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: You can describe the result of the stated task and choose one useful next attempt. Completion records your own practice reflection.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: If the harmony collapses into the lead, mute the lead, sing the harmony from its anchor notes, then restore the lead at lower volume. Repeat a smaller version on another fresh attempt rather than forcing the checkpoint.
selfAssessment.proves: I rehearsed the supplied study arrangement and compared microphone distance or phrasing on separate takes. This is a self-report, not an automatic assessment.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: An automatic pitch, rhythm, register, tone, or safety result. Two simultaneous vocal parts, harmony accuracy, blend, independence, absence of a register break, or vocal health; the detector returns one fundamental per frame.
